references.text: God did not lead the people back to Egypt, but away from it, which underscores the prohibition against returning
Moses assured the people that they would never see the Egyptians again, confirming that a return to Egypt was contrary to God's will
The people wanted to return to Egypt, which was rebellion against God and violated His command
Solomon gathered many horses from Egypt, in direct violation of this command that the king should not acquire many horses
Solomon had forty thousand stalls for horses, showing a breach of the prohibition against acquiring many horses
Isaiah warns against seeking help from Egypt and trusting in horses, reflecting the prohibition in Deuteronomy
The prophet warns against going down to Egypt for protection, which breaks God's command
Hosea warns against trusting in Assyria and horses, and against returning to Egypt
Jeremiah warns the people against fleeing to Egypt and prophesies judgment on those who do so
